goals: Characterize how peak SWE varies along the Wenatchee elevation gradient (mechanistic gradient goal)
Validate modeled peak SWE against the 5 in-domain SNOTEL stations (validation goal)
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (acting through orographic precip and temperature)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates SWE (H2OSNO) in default output, and NLDAS-2 forcing varies precip/temperature with location and elevation, so an elevation-stratified column set samples the snow gradient directly. SNOTEL SWE is available in-domain for co-located validation.

answerable: The shape of the peak-SWE vs elevation gradient across the basin at ~12 km forcing resolution
Co-located comparison of modeled vs observed peak SWE at the 5 SNOTEL stations (bias, RMSE, timing)

not_answerable.aspect: Accurate peak-SWE magnitude at high, terrain-exposed ridgetop SNOTEL stations
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 is 0.125° (~12 km) with no within-cell lapse rate; a 2683 m-relief basin is under-resolved, so high-elevation cells average over lower surrounding terrain and systematically underestimate ridgetop SWE.
not_answerable.needs: elevation-downscaled / sub-12 km forcing with within-cell lapse rate

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified along elevation, with validation columns pinned to observations
sampling_strategy.n_justification: One driver (elevation) resolved into 5 bands spanning 187-2870 m; 5 base columns cover the bands with 2 extra placed in the 1200-1800 m rain-snow transition where dSWE/dz and warming sensitivity are largest. This is the smallest set that resolves the gradient shape without redundant sampling.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Space exploratory columns to bracket the full relief (one near the 187 m valley floor, one near the 2870 m crest) and oversample the rain-snow transition band; keep them off the SNOTEL cells so they add gradient coverage rather than duplicate validation points. Forcing differences among columns must come from distinct NLDAS cells to represent the orographic gradient.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light: 2 replicate columns in the rain-snow transition band (different NLDAS cells) to see spread where sensitivity is highest; elsewhere single columns.

sampling_plan.reason: Anchors the low, rain-dominated end of the gradient where peak SWE should be near zero/ephemeral.
Captures onset of seasonal snow accumulation on the lower slopes.
Oversampled band where dSWE/dz and warming sensitivity peak; isolates the steepest part of the gradient.
Brackets the deep/persistent-snow high end and tests forcing-resolution limits at ridgetop.
Co-located with the 5 SNOTEL SWE stations to validate modeled peak SWE against observations.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place a column in the NLDAS cell containing each SNOTEL station and compare modeled annual peak SWE and its timing to observed, over overlapping winters within 1980-2018
validation_design.metric: peak-SWE bias and RMSE, plus date-of-peak difference; expect negative (under) bias at the highest/most exposed stations from 12 km averaging

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing, multi-winter period (multiple years within 1980-2018 overlapping SNOTEL record), native SSURGO soil per column

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled / sub-12 km forcing with within-cell lapse rate
requires_capabilities.why: Resolve peak-SWE magnitude at ridgetop stations that 12 km NLDAS cells under-resolve
requires_capabilities.blocks: Accurate high-elevation SWE magnitude and unbiased ridgetop validation

requires_capabilities.why: Brief gives station count but not lat/lon; needed to place co-located validation columns and assign correct NLDAS cells

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL SWE observation ingest & peak-SWE extraction
requires_capabilities.why: Compute observed annual peak SWE and date-of-peak for the metric
Assign columns to elevation bands and select representative points

assumptions: The basin lies within CONUS so NLDAS-2 (elevation-varying at 12 km) is the forcing; if any point falls outside CONUS it would revert to non-elevation-resolved Qian and break the gradient premise.
SWE is a seasonal fast state, so no multi-year water-table spin-up is required; a multi-winter forcing period suffices for a peak-SWE climatology.
SNOTEL stations are distributed across elevation, not clustered at one band; if clustered, gradient validation is weaker.
open_questions: What are the 5 SNOTEL station coordinates and elevations, and what years do they cover for overlap selection?
Should peak SWE be compared as a single-year event or as a multi-year climatological mean/percentile?
Are the SNOTEL stations spread across the elevation range or concentrated in the mid-high bands?
